subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Halo Effect
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Halo Effect usable.

hook.text: Attractive defendants get lighter sentences. Good looks signal nothing about guilt, yet juries are swayed.

buildup.text: The halo effect: one positive trait (beauty, fame, confidence) colors judgment of unrelated traits.

discovery.text: Edward Thorndike first documented it in 1920: military officers rated soldiers as good at everything or bad at everything.

twist.text: It works in reverse too. One negative trait—a lisp, a stain—can make everything about a person seem worse.

climax.text: Brands exploit halos: Apple's design reputation creates a halo that covers its pricing and restrictions.

punchline.text: One trait shouldn't color the whole picture. But it does.

quiz.question: What is the halo effect?
options: One positive trait biases judgment of unrelated traits
